stem: What is the purpose of competency validation for clinical staff?

options.A: Document attendance at education sessions without determining whether the staff member can safely perform the assigned task.
options.B: Validate through a defined process that the staff member can synthesize and correctly apply required knowledge and technical skills to perform assigned responsibilities safely.
options.C: Replace education and training because competency can be validated without foundational knowledge or technical skills.
options.D: Evaluate personality traits rather than the knowledge, skills, and ability required for role-specific clinical responsibilities.

rationale: The Joint Commission distinguishes education, training, and competency. Education provides theoretical knowledge, training develops technical skills, and competency adds the ability to synthesize and correctly apply that knowledge and those skills to a task. Competency assessment is the organization's defined process for validating that ability. B is therefore correct. Attendance alone does not establish competence, competency does not replace education/training, and personality traits are not the focus of this clinical competency definition.
educational_objective: Differentiate competency validation from education or training by recognizing that competency assessment confirms the ability to correctly apply required knowledge and technical skills to assigned clinical tasks.
source_document_title: Standards FAQ — Competency Assessment vs Education and Training
source_locator: Definitions of Education, Training, and Competency; paragraph beginning 'Competency differs from education and training'; paragraph defining competency assessment
source_claim_supported: Competency incorporates knowledge, technical skills, and ability, and competency assessment validates through a defined process that an individual can perform a task consistent with education and training.

source_original.stem: What is the purpose of competency validation for clinical staff?

options.A: Measure attendance at education sessions without determining whether the learner can perform the task
options.B: Confirm that staff can correctly apply required knowledge and technical skills to perform assigned tasks safely
options.C: Replace all education and training because competency can be assessed without foundational knowledge or skills
options.D: Evaluate personality traits rather than the ability to perform role-specific clinical responsibilities safely

source_original.rationale: The Joint Commission distinguishes competency from education and training: competency includes the ability to synthesize and correctly apply knowledge and technical skills. Assessment validates that the individual can perform required tasks.
source_original.source_detail: Standards FAQ: competency includes knowledge, technical skills, and ability; last updated June 24, 2026; accessed 2026-08-14.

correction_summary: Verified the Joint Commission FAQ's June 24, 2026 update, made the defined validation process and knowledge-skill-ability distinction explicit, and preserved easy difficulty.

audit_findings.source_authority: The Joint Commission current Standards FAQ; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.claim_audit: The source directly defines education, training, competency, and competency assessment; the final answer mirrors the ability-to-apply construct without adding unsupported requirements.

distractor_audit.A: Attendance is education/training participation, not validation of ability.
distractor_audit.C: Competency builds on education and training rather than replacing them.
distractor_audit.D: Personality is not the defined competency construct.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B contains knowledge, technical skill, ability, and validation of performance.
audit_findings.cueing: All alternatives describe assessment purposes; no second plausible definition remains.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care retained because this is supervision/competence within safe care delivery.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read the June 2026 FAQ, challenged whether 'safe' was directly supportable, confirmed the source explicitly ties competency attributes to delivering safe care and correctly performing technical tasks, and retained B as uniquely correct.
